disposition_reason: Table 3 prints fresh-weight means of 13 elements including Cd, Cr, Ni and Pb for four wild and two cultivated blueberry samples.

study.design: compositional survey of wild and cultivated blueberry fruit samples
study.origin: wild: three pine forest sites in Mazovia, central Poland (W1-W3); cultivated: garden plot outside Warsaw (C2)
study.market: W4 and C1 bought at a local marketplace/market, Poland
study.method: HNO3/HClO4 digestion on hot plate; ICP-OES (iCAP 6000)
study.lod_text: LOQ (mg/kg): Al 1.0, Ca 0.2, Cd 0.0003, Cr 0.03, Cu 0.5, Fe 0.5, Mg 2.0, Mn 0.05, Na 5.0, Ni 0.2, Pb 0.5, Zn 0.3 (Table 1); K not listed
study.qa: CRMs Mixed Polish Herbs INGT-MPH-2 and Leaves of Poplar NCS DC 73350 agreed with certified values (Table 2); spike recoveries 87-109% (data not shown)

controls.control: cultivated highbush blueberry versus wild blueberry
controls.outcome: Cd 0.013 and 0.040 mg/kg (C1, C2) vs 0.001-0.004 mg/kg (W1-W4); authors link C2 to higher garden soil Cd 0.398 mg/kg vs 0.041-0.087 mg/kg at wild sites

controls.control: hot-water extraction (infusion) of fresh versus dried berries
controls.outcome: extraction percentages figure-only (Fig. 1); authors state leaching of Pb and Cd from fresh and dried wild blueberries was very little

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 maximum levels for berries as cited by the authors

unresolved: Pb means (0.266-0.556 mg/kg) are below the stated Pb LOQ of 0.5 mg/kg except W1; Cu means are all below the Cu LOQ of 0.5 mg/kg; Cr in W3 and C2 and Ni in C1 are below their LOQs. Values kept as printed with integrity flags.
Authors state Cd and Pb are below the EU limits of 0.05 and 0.2 mg/kg, but all printed Pb means exceed 0.2 mg/kg.
Each sample is a single lot analyzed in triplicate; n = 3 refers to determinations, not independent samples.
